newsitem.title: THAILAND: Royalist soldiers return to Cambodia after fleeing.
newsitem.headline: Royalist soldiers return to Cambodia after fleeing.

text.p: Some 360 troops loyal to Cambodia's ousted premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh returned to Cambodia after fleeing to Thailand last week, and thousands of refugees were expected to follow, Thai officials said on Monday.
The royalist troops had fled fighting in northwestern Cambodia late last week and were allowed into Thailand after being disarmed, Thai Colonel Anuphong Paochinda told reporters.
He said the royalists returned to their Cambodian villages over the weekend.
A large number of weapons, including AK and M-16 rifles, mortars, submachines guns and ammunition were left behind in Thailand.
About 3,600 Cambodian refugees who left Thailand to escape fighting between the royalists and troops loyal to strongman Hun Sen, were expected to go home on Tuesday or Wednesday, Anuphong said.
"The fighting situation died down in the areas and the Cambodian officials have agreed to take these people back," he said.

Factional fighting in several small villages in northwestern Cambodia late last week forced between 5,000-6,000 people to flee to Aranyaprathet district in eastern Thailand. Some of them returned to Cambodia shortly after crossing into Thailand.
Thai military officials on the border said on Friday that Hun Sen's forces had captured O'Bei Choan and its 200 royalist defenders had withdrawn into the bush.

Friday's movement of refugees was the first time Cambodians had been allowed across the border since before U.N.-sponsored elections in Cambodia in 1993. Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed an uneasy coalition after that poll.
Thai officials said they decided to allow the refugees in because they had nowhere to go and had to escape the fighting.
Sporadic battles have been continuing in parts of Cambodia since a bloody July 5-6 power grab by Hun Sen in the capital Phnom Penh.
Thai officials said the fighting appeared to have calmed down after Hun Sen met three foreign ministers from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Saturday.

Hun Sen and the ASEAN ministers agreed on the need to end conflict in Cambodia. The ASEAN ministers raised the question of a role for Ranariddh but Hun Sen on Monday ruled out any talks with the prince, saying Ranariddh had to stand trial first for his alleged crimes.
